The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Kalshi turns to small businesses as legal battles threaten forecasts on sports. The prediction market is pitching protection against tariffs, weather and other business risks as courts challenge its ability to offer sports wagers. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin 'death cross' is coming. Here's what happened after previous 13.. Your day-ahead look for Nov. 27, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin on course to end seven-week losing streak while trailing stock rebound. Bitcoin (BTC) has risen 1.8% since midnight UTC to around $61,600 and is on course to end seven straight weekly losses. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Bitcoin's Thanksgiving gains prove fleeting. Stocks are broadly higher, but bitcoin has slipped back near $60,000, reversing a turkey day advance. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Next ECB chief favors tokenized bank deposits over stablecoins and bitcoin. Pablo Hernández de Cos, chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde, favors blockchain-based banking and has warned against private digital currencies and banks holding bitcoin. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Injective asks SEC to allow order books for tokenized stock trading. The regulator's rules favor one type of blockchain trading system, leaving platforms built on Injective out, the developer said. It wants the SEC to open stock trading to order-book systems. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $59,689 with a -1.33% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,658.48 with a -2.21% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: US Bitcoin ETF Adds 4,614 BTC as Ethereum ETF Sees 23,039 ETH Inflow — Coincu
items.description:
Do Ethereum ETF inflows affect market sentiment?

Ethereum ETF inflows contribute to sentiment but are currently smaller in magnitude than Bitcoin ETF flows. Today’s $51.38 million Ethereum inflow, while positive, represents a fraction of the Bitcoin figure. As Ethereum ETF products mature and potentially gain features like staking yield, their flow data may carry increasing weight in sentiment analysis. [...] Bitcoin ETF flows serve as a proxy for regulated investment demand. Because U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs are accessible through standard brokerage accounts, their flow data captures demand from institutional allocators, financial advisors, and retail investors who prefer regulated vehicles over direct crypto custody. The scale of flows, such as today’s $334.63 million, reflects meaningful capital allocation decisions. Movements in crypto-adjacent equities often track alongside these ETF flow trends. [...] U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net inflow of 4,614 BTC on April 10, 2026, while Ethereum ETFs absorbed 23,039 ETH in the same session, marking a day of synchronized institutional demand across both major crypto assets.

The figures come from blockchain analytics tracker Lookonchain, which posted its daily ETF flow update showing the Bitcoin inflow was worth approximately $334.63 million at the time of reporting.

items.description: That sets up today's thesis. Ether isn't trading on the AI equity bounce or Bitcoin's options expiry. It's trading on its own supply overhang. U.S. spot Ether ETFs have posted outflows for eight straight sessions, totaling $1.3 billion in November. BitMine, the largest corporate treasury, keeps buying, but at a fraction of the rate ETFs are redeeming. The market cap of $206.6 billion to $211.6 billion reflects a token losing relative share to Bitcoin. [...] ETF redemptions are the main reason Ether can't hold a rally. U.S. spot Ether ETFs have recorded net outflows for eight straight trading days. November's cumulative net outflow is about $1.3 billion. That makes it the third-largest monthly outflow for the products, behind October 2026's $1.61 billion and November 2025's $1.42 billion. items.description:
That sets up today's thesis. IBIT is the center of the largest institutional exit from Bitcoin since spot ETFs launched. US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost a record $5.39 billion in November through Wednesday, beating June's previous record by $880 million. IBIT carried 85% of that selling. Each dollar of IBIT redemptions forces authorized participants to sell Bitcoin, which pushes the price down, which lowers IBIT, which triggers more redemptions. The question for IBIT is when that loop breaks. [...] On Wednesday, November 25, outflows picked up again to $453 million. IBIT lost $329.7 million, the Mini Trust $60.1 million, BITB $18.2 million, ARKB $14.9 million and GBTC $13.9 million. None of the 12 funds recorded an inflow. Bitcoin fell to $57,243.98 that day after the hot core PCE print.

The pattern is clear. Outflows slowed on Tuesday, then rose again on Wednesday when macro data turned hawkish. That shows the selling is tied to Fed expectations, not only to Bitcoin's own momentum. [...] November is now the worst month in the history of US spot Bitcoin ETFs. Through Wednesday, November 25, net outflows reached $5.39 billion. That passes June 2026's previous record of $4.51 billion by $880 million, with two sessions left: today's shortened day and Monday, November 30. For 2026 as a whole, spot Bitcoin ETFs now show net outflows of $5.02 billion. That compares with $35.24 billion of net inflows in 2024 and $21.37 billion in 2025. November erased all of 2026's earlier gains.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: Will a new law make cryptocurrency safer? - Harvard Law School | Harvard Law School
items.description:
Howell Jackson: Stablecoins are a unique part of the cryptocurrency ecosystem in that their value, at least under the regulatory structure adopted in the GENIUS Act, are derived from a specific pool of safe assets that have been defined and need to be held in segregated accounts and custodied in a prescribed way. The new law requires that stablecoin issuers have reserves on hand to back 100% of the value of stablecoins in circulating. That’s very different from, say, Bitcoin or Ether, whose [...] On July 18, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act, the first major piece of American legislation aimed at regulating cryptocurrency. The law, boosted by a bipartisan group of legislators, targets stablecoins, a kind of digital currency whose value is pegged to a fiat currency, most commonly the U.S. dollar. [...] Finally, there will be a huge amount of work, as a regulatory matter, in rolling out the GENIUS Act. The law had many different flavors of how you could organize your stablecoins under state law, under federal law, as the subsidiaries of a bank, as a separate federal charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. It’s going to be interesting to watch it all unfold.
